matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); do not rotate the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, verify that its orientation remains unchanged.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I and placing it as a horizontal bar, thereby rotating its orientation.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, enforce that the total number of sticks stays constant.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from a V and not placing it anywhere, leaving the V incomplete.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, every symbol must be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, check that each character still forms a recognized symbol.
matchstick.example: Turning a V into a shape with three diagonals, which is not a recognized Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate transformed equation, compute its numeric values before finalizing.
matchstick.example: Accepting 'XIII = VI + II' without checking that 13 ≠ 8, missing the arithmetic error.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals, i.e., you cannot leave a V or X with only one diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a diagonal from a V or X, ensure the source character still has two diagonals after the move.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from a V and moving it to another character, leaving the V with only one diagonal.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different position inside the same numeral, altering its shape while keeping the character a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a value needs to be adjusted without affecting other symbols, consider repositioning a stick within the same character.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to a different character instead of repositioning it within the V to become an X.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; you cannot alter, add to, or remove from it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Never consider moving a stick from or to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one of the two horizontal bars of '=', turning it into a '-' sign.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one character to a different character, altering both; ensure both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single‑character change cannot achieve equality, consider moving a stick between characters.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to an I, turning '+' into '-' but leaving the I as an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' (case‑insensitive, whitespace‑collapsed).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have the correct equation, output it using the required prefix and format.
matchstick.example: Providing the answer as 'XIII = XI + II' without the required 'Correct version of the equation:' prefix.

matchstick.title: V↔X conversion via diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: When a V or X appears, consider moving one of its diagonal sticks within the same character to change V↔X, adjusting its value by ±5 while preserving the two‑diagonal structure.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the numeric discrepancy between the two sides of the equation is exactly 5, try converting a V to X (or X to V) inside the same numeral.
matchstick.example: Attempting to fix a mismatch by moving a diagonal from a V to another numeral, which breaks the V, instead of repositioning it within the V to become an X.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and forgets to check the numeric values of the resulting Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides of the final equation to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality before submitting.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a stick from '+' can unintentionally create an operator that is not '+' or '-', such as a lone vertical line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When altering an operator, ensure the remaining sticks form a valid operator (+, -, =) after the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs the equation without the required prefix or with extra whitespace, causing the parser to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: End the response with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', using uppercase and collapsing whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it elsewhere, violating the one‑stick‑move rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick you take must be placed on another character; double‑check that the total number of sticks stays constant.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral (X or V) by moving a stick away
matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a diagonal from X or V leaves the source numeral with only one diagonal, which is not a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only reposition diagonals within X or V, or move a whole diagonal to another character while simultaneously adding a diagonal to keep the source valid.
